_comment: Seed-level SPECS for `dotnet run --project Tools/LevelTool -- generate`. Every level has 4 open slots + 2 locked ones (R20). The oval: rows round it, width bottles per row (default 4), pickRows = the pick zone in front of the slots (track positions 0..pickRows-1; rows >= 2*pickRows + 6). feeders: where each queue joins (mergeAt = its ENTRANCE, where its head row stands; outside the pick zone; at most 2 feeders): a queue row takes the free belt row nearest its entrance, within 2 rows either way. Feeders read left to right in belt order: with B = (rows - 2*pickRows)/2 bend rows, they come down from the top: a RIGHT queue enters at rows - B/2 - 3 (its ramp lands on the right bend 3 rows further on), a LEFT one at its mirror image rows + pickRows - right mergeAt - 2 (drawn as the mirror of the right one), and how many bottles it carries (whole rows: a multiple of width). The belt starts EMPTY; every bottle waits in a feeder, and a feeder puts one whole row of one colour on the belt at a time. The tool paints colours and builds the tray queues (solvable by construction) and writes Assets/CapsChaos/Content/LevelConfig/. greed: 1 = easy (trays match what is on the belt), 0 = tense. clustering: 1 = long blocks of one colour.

levels.name: First Caps
levels.notes: Teaches: tap a tray, bottles fly in, the box ships.

levels.name: Three Belts
levels.notes: Teaches: three tray belts, the belt steps forward.

levels.name: Round and Round
levels.notes: Teaches: only bottles passing in front of the slots are picked; the rest come round again.

levels.name: Joining In
levels.notes: Teaches: the queue joins the oval wherever a picked bottle left a gap.

levels.name: Two Queues
levels.notes: Teaches: two queues join the oval at different points.

levels.name: Tight Slots
levels.notes: First level where a careless order jams the slots.

levels.name: Rush Hour
levels.notes: Approximates the reference video: one long queue feeding a crowded oval.

levels.name: Hundred Rows
levels.notes: 100 queue rows (400 bottles) across two feeders.

levels.name: Triangle
levels.notes: A triangular loop (apex up): the pick zone is its base, the queues merge into the middle of its slanted sides.
